data.title: Designing Homes for the Kerala Monsoon
data.author: KATIC Design Studio
data.excerpt: Deep eaves, raised plinths and planted courtyards: how architecture can welcome the rain instead of fighting it.

body.text: For four months a year, Kerala homes live with heavy rain, high humidity and soft, diffused light. The best houses here don’t resist the monsoon — they are designed around it.
Start with the roof

Generous overhangs protect walls and openings from driving rain and keep rooms cool through the rest of the year. Sloped roofs with well-sized gutters move water away quickly, and a raised plinth keeps the floor dry during heavy downpours.

body.caption: Deep overhangs shading the south garden elevation.

body.text: Let the air move
Aligned openings, courtyards and high-level vents keep air moving and help with humidity. Cross-ventilated rooms dry out faster, smell fresher and need less mechanical cooling.

items: Overhangs of at least 900 mm on exposed elevations
Courtyards with drainage designed for peak rainfall
Breathable finishes such as lime plaster on external walls
Covered transitions between indoor and outdoor spaces

body.text: Designed this way, the monsoon becomes part of daily life: the sound of rain in the courtyard, soft light in the living room and a home that stays comfortable all year.

data.title: Planning an Interior That Lasts
data.author: KATIC Interior
data.excerpt: Five decisions that make the difference between an interior that dates quickly and one that ages well.

body.text: Interiors that last are planned around routines, not trends. Before choosing colours or furniture, map how each room will actually be used at different times of day.
Plan storage first
Most clutter is a storage problem. Built-in storage designed at the start keeps rooms calm and saves floor space.
Choose fewer, better materials
A tight palette of durable materials — stone, timber, lime and metal — reads as calm and ages well. Sample everything in the actual room light before you decide.

body.caption: Teak joinery along the courtyard edge.

body.text: Layer the lighting
Combine ambient, task and accent lighting so each room works for reading, cooking, gathering and resting.

data.title: Choosing Natural Stone for Kerala Homes
data.author: KATIC Interior
data.excerpt: Kota, granite, laterite and limestone compared for durability, comfort underfoot and maintenance in a humid climate.

body.text: Stone is one of the most durable materials you can choose, but not every stone suits every room or climate.
Kota stone
Cool underfoot, quietly tonal and very hard wearing — ideal for verandas and living areas. A honed finish reduces slipperiness in wet weather.
Granite
Dense and stain-resistant, granite is a reliable choice for kitchen counters and external steps.
Laterite
Kerala’s traditional building stone gives walls warmth and texture, and breathes well in humid conditions.
Whatever you choose, ask for large samples and see them wet and dry before deciding.

data.title: A Construction Quality Checklist for Homeowners
data.author: KATIC Infrastructure
data.excerpt: What to check at each stage of construction — from foundations to finishing — to make sure your home is built as drawn.

body.text: Quality on site is the result of many small checks made at the right time. Here is what we inspect at each stage.
Foundations and structure

items: Excavation depth and soil bearing confirmed
Reinforcement size, spacing and cover checked before every pour
Concrete cube tests recorded for each pour

body.text: Services
Electrical and plumbing routes are checked against the drawings before walls are closed, and pressure tests are carried out on all water lines.
Finishing
Plaster lines, floor levels, tile joints and paint coats are inspected room by room, and a snag list is shared before handover.

data.title: What “Turnkey” Really Means
data.author: KATIC Design Studio
data.excerpt: One team, one contract, one programme. How turnkey delivery works and when it is the right choice for your project.

body.text: In a turnkey project, one team takes responsibility for design, approvals, construction, interiors and handover. You approve the brief, the budget and key decisions — we coordinate everything else.
Why it works
Fewer hand-offs mean fewer gaps between trades, faster decisions and a design that is built as intended.
When to choose it
Turnkey suits clients who want a single point of accountability and limited time to manage consultants and contractors.

data.title: Renovating an Older Home Without Losing Its Character
data.author: KATIC Design Studio
data.excerpt: How to decide what to keep, what to change and what to fix first when you renovate an older building.

body.text: Older buildings often have qualities that are hard to recreate: thick walls, high ceilings, mature trees. Good renovation keeps these and fixes what no longer works.
Survey before you design
A structural and services survey reveals damp, cracks and outdated wiring before they become expensive surprises.
Fix the envelope first
Roof, waterproofing and drainage come before finishes. A dry building is the foundation of every other improvement.

data.title: Low-Maintenance Gardens for the Tropics
data.author: KATIC Design Studio
data.excerpt: Native planting, shade and smart drainage for gardens that look good all year with little upkeep.

body.text: A tropical garden can be lush without being demanding. The key is choosing plants and materials that suit the climate.
Plant native
Native species cope with heavy rain and dry spells, attract birds and insects, and need far less care.
Design for water
Permeable paving, swales and rain gardens let water soak in instead of flooding paths and foundations.

data.title: Why Design Leads Value in Real Estate
data.author: KATIC Developers
data.excerpt: Better light, better plans and better materials: why design-led developments hold their value for longer.

body.text: Buyers notice light, air and good planning, even when they can’t name them. Developments designed around these qualities sell faster and age better.
Plan for daily life
Well-proportioned rooms, cross-ventilation and usable balconies matter more over time than headline amenities.
Specify for the long term
Durable materials reduce maintenance costs for owners and keep buildings looking good for longer.

data.title: A Pre-Monsoon Maintenance Checklist
data.author: KATIC Care
data.excerpt: Ten checks to make before the rains arrive, from roof gutters to garden drainage.

body.text: A few hours of inspection before the monsoon can prevent months of damp and repairs.

items: Check roof tiles and sheets for cracks
Inspect terrace waterproofing and parapet joints
Test sump pumps and outdoor electrical points
Check for damp patches on walls
Service exterior timber with oil or sealant

body.text: KATIC Care offers pre-monsoon inspections as part of every maintenance plan.
